mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative when GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive when unemployment exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate alongside falling unemployment indicates tightening, negatively impacting S&P 500.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive despite rising FEDFUNDS and falling UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing industrial production growth in late expansion signals weaker S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive despite slowing INDPRO growth.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation leads to tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive when inflation is high.

mechanism_narrative: Declining housing starts indicate weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive when housing starts are below 1000.

mechanism_narrative: Employment growth with slowing retail sales indicates consumer weakness, negatively impacting S&P 500.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive despite employment growth and retail sales slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate indicates tight monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive when FEDFUNDS exceed 4%.
